title: When the draft runs late
hook: The draft overruns by five minutes.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Distinguish planned slack from overlapping bookings.

objective: Distinguish planned slack from overlapping bookings.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: The draft overruns by five minutes. The draft runs 5 minutes over. Which plan has no clash with the call? Correct option: Gap, call at 25. All fixture labels and durations are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Stipulated exercise fixture in studyCatalog.ts. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 8), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): With the event applied (draft 0-25): A call 20-35 overlaps 5 min; B call 25-40, notes 45-55, 0 min. Only "Gap, call at 25" has no clash. Stipulated data.

claims.text: A gap can absorb up to its length of delay in this schedule. It is a stated allowance, not a guarantee about real tasks.

claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): Numbers re-run over every prediction and every Yours state; 0 mismatches between table and reveal. The column order in this text is one path: the reveal quotes optionToMode[prediction] first, so some learners read the same two sentences in the other order, and a Yours sentence is appended when the learner moved the stage to a third state (its numbers match the Yours column). Keyed prediction (2) reads the "5-min gap" sentence first. Note: "Gap before call" is the planned gap (ignores the overrun), so a Yours layout can read "gap 1 min; overlap 4 min", which is true but worth a look by interaction-designer.

recall.question: A call booked 9:00–9:30 may run up to ten minutes over. When should the next task start so an overrun cannot collide?
recall.why: A gap absorbs delay up to its length; ten minutes of overrun needs a ten-minute gap, so 9:40.
